fragments.text: Hello everyone. First and foremost, I'd like to thank the organizing committee for asking me to contribute to the AI or AI conference. It is great to see different actors, academics and practitioners contributing to this topic on AI is used for information access, which is a key pillar in democracy, human rights, freedom of expression and for better transparency and accountability of public services, among other things. This year, I'd like to discuss briefly on deliberative democracy, deliberative democracy is a school of thought in political theory that claims that political decisions should be the product of fair and reasonable discussions and debate among citizens. In deliberations, citizens exchange arguments and consider different claims that are designed to secure the public good.

fragments.text: Through these conversations, citizens can come to an argument about what procedure action or policy will best produce the public good. In this process, there needs to be access to information. First, governments and decision makers need to access information from the public deliberation and make sense of it so that they can respond to it. Second, the public also need access to the results of the deliberations because not all deliberations will be happening at the same time or at the same place. This ensures that there is a level of transparency and accountability in the process without which democracy is threatened. To deliver this, some governments are now applying a new class of deliberative technologies. These digital tools support public discussions on policy issues and encourage citizens to participate and synthesize a wide range of insights.
